evidence: Receiving online DO2 sensor at t=52 h: ~9.71 mg/L, stable across recent samples (9.7–10.3 mg/L band)
Receiving delayed P assays: 1.13 g/L (t=35.8), 3.15 g/L (t=47.8) — normal growth trajectory
Forward model, strong_feed_reduction: product mass 621.5 kg, post-decision min DO 8.50 mg/L, 0 h below limit
Forward model sensitivity (5/5 feasible): mass 616.3–627.3 kg, min DO 7.22–9.50 mg/L
Comparison runs: keep 576.3 kg / min DO 6.44; reduce_feed 595.5 / 7.27; combined 595.5 / 7.74; increase_air 576.3 / 6.67
args.rationale: Current receiving batch at t=52 h is stable and well-oxygenated (DO2 ≈ 9.7 mg/L, trend normal, latest P assay 3.15 g/L). No oxygen-constraint violation is predicted under any candidate action; stop is unwarranted. The physics tool, though source-calibrated and imperfect, consistently ranks feed-reduction plans above keep/increase_air on BOTH the hard constraint margin and product mass retention. strong_feed_reduction is predicted to deliver the highest product mass (621.5 kg vs 576.3 kg for keep) and the highest minimum post-decision DO (8.50 mg/L nominal, 7.22–9.50 across all 5 sensitivity members, all feasible). Since every bounded intervention is feasible, the decision priority reduces to product-mass retention, which favors the strongest feed reduction. Model mismatch risk is mitigated by the wide DO margin: even the worst sensitivity member (7.22 mg/L) exceeds the 2 mg/L limit by >3.6x, so forecast error of several mg/L would not cause a violation.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is calibrated to source batches, not the hidden receiving realization; the ~19 kg mass gain over keep depends on model structure (reduced feed lowering dilution/volume while product formation continues). Sensitivity members are not probabilities. DO margin is large, so oxygen-constraint risk is low, but product-mass benefit carries moderate model-mismatch uncertainty. Observations themselves give no indication of distress, so keep would also be acceptable; strong_feed_reduction is chosen as the supported feasible plan maximizing retained mass.
